note: Adapted from the revision of Sands 1965 (where the species was originally described as new), in English; the alate and the soldier are described, with no separate worker. The OCR mistook decimal points for hyphens (0-88 is 0.88, I-10 is 1.10), restored here by order of magnitude; every figure and reading was checked item by item. The species was erected as a new species contrasted with E. bipartitus; type locality Njili, Congo.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate head capsule brownish, with pale yellowish brown patches on the frons, the postclypeus and the antennae, labrum yellow; pronotum and meso- and metanotum brown, the remaining thoracic sclerites and the legs yellow; abdominal tergites brown, sternites yellowish brown. Differs from E. bipartitus in the ocelli lying a little farther from the eye, the different shape of the frontal mark and the more broadly rounded posterior margin of the head capsule; the soldier has a narrow nasus and more head setae. The differences from E. aquilinus, E. convergens and E. undulans are given under each of those species.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Posterior margin of the head capsule behind the eyes evenly rounded, slightly less than a semicircle, slightly flared at the eye margin; frontal mark paler than the head capsule, minute, triangular or forming three spots arranged in a triangle; compound eyes oval, slightly protruding from the sides of the head, markedly protruding relative to their own diameter and large relative to the head width, eye width index 2.6—2.9; ocelli small, oval, separated from the compound eye by about half their minimum diameter or a little more; postclypeus moderately inflated, about twice as wide as long, anterior margin wavy, posterior margin convex and evenly rounded; antennae 15-segmented, segments II, IV and V subequal, III shorter. Head setae fairly uniform and dense, but not yet forming a fur; the setae of the pronotum and abdomen are similar and longer at the margins of the sclerites. Measurements (3 individuals, 2 localities, mm): head width (across the eyes) 0.88—0.94; maximum diameter of the compound eye 0.33—0.35; ocellus 0.08—0.09 × 0.11—0.13; ocellus to eye 0.04—0.05; pronotum width 0.73—0.79; pronotum length 0.49—0.54; hind tibia length 1.10—1.23.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow to yellow, nasus orange yellow to orange, the rest of the body wall pale yellow. Head capsule in frontal view weakly constricted behind the antennae, the posterior margin evenly rounded or slightly angularly rounded; nasus narrow, weakly conical. In lateral view the dorsal margin wavy, with a distinct boss at the base of the nasus and dropping rapidly behind it; the highest point lies directly above the middle of the postgenal plate. Antennal segments II, III and V subequal, IV shorter, the dorsal margin of the antennal socket often with a small ridge. The conspicuous head setae are 3 pairs (6 in all) in a transverse row at the constriction in front of the base of the nasus, and likewise 3 pairs (6 in all) on the posterolateral lobes behind the constriction. Measurements (7 individuals, 3 localities, mm): head length (to the tip of the nasus) 1.25—1.40 (mean 1.34); head width 0.61—0.73 (mean 0.67); head capsule depth 0.38—0.46 (mean 0.42); pronotum width 0.34—0.38; pronotum length 0.13—0.14; hind tibia length 0.71—0.83 (mean 0.74).
